quizzes.title: Know Your India
quizzes.description: National symbols, state capitals and famous places from across India.

questions.q: What is the national animal of India?
questions.note: The tiger replaced the lion as the national animal in 1973.

questions.q: The Tropic of Capricorn passes through India.
questions.note: It is the Tropic of Cancer that crosses India, through eight states.

questions.q: What is the capital of Karnataka?
questions.note: Bengaluru is often called the Silicon Valley of India.

questions.q: Which Indian state is known as God's Own Country?
questions.note: The slogan comes from a Kerala Tourism campaign.

questions.q: What is the national flower of India?
questions.note: The lotus grows in muddy water yet blooms clean, a symbol of purity.

questions.q: The Sundarbans mangrove forest lies in which Indian state?
questions.note: It is home to the Royal Bengal tiger and extends into Bangladesh.

questions.q: The Ashoka Chakra on India's national flag has 24 spokes.
questions.note: The chakra is navy blue and sits in the centre of the white band.

questions.q: Which city is known as the Pink City?
questions.note: Jodhpur is the Blue City and Udaipur the City of Lakes.

questions.q: What is the capital of Maharashtra?
questions.note: Nagpur hosts the state legislature's winter session.

questions.q: Which is the largest Indian state by area?
questions.note: Rajasthan has been the largest since Chhattisgarh was carved out of Madhya Pradesh in 2000.

quizzes.title: Festivals & Traditions
quizzes.description: Harvest festivals, classical dance and celebrations from every corner of India.

questions.q: Onam is mainly celebrated in which state?
questions.note: Onam welcomes the legendary King Mahabali back to his land.

questions.q: Which harvest festival is celebrated in Tamil Nadu in mid-January?
questions.note: Pongal is named after the sweet rice dish cooked to mark it.

questions.q: Durga Puja in Kolkata is on UNESCO's list of Intangible Cultural Heritage.
questions.note: It was added to the list in 2021.

questions.q: Bharatanatyam is a classical dance form from which state?
questions.note: Kathakali comes from Kerala, Odissi from Odisha and Kuchipudi from Andhra Pradesh.

questions.q: Which spring festival is famous for people throwing coloured powder and water?
questions.note: Holi celebrates the arrival of spring and the victory of good over evil.

questions.q: Bihu is the most important festival of which state?
questions.note: Assam celebrates three Bihus a year; Rongali Bihu marks the new year in April.

questions.q: Eid al-Fitr marks the beginning of the holy month of Ramadan.
questions.note: Eid al-Fitr marks the end of Ramadan's month of fasting.

questions.q: The Hornbill Festival is held every December in which state?
questions.note: It is held at Kisama near Kohima and showcases all of Nagaland's tribes.

questions.q: Which festival celebrates the bond of siblings with a thread tied on a brother's wrist?
questions.note: Accept Rakhi.

questions.q: Which festival also marks the founding of the Khalsa by Guru Gobind Singh in 1699?
questions.note: Vaisakhi is also a spring harvest festival in Punjab.

quizzes.title: Sporting India
quizzes.description: Historic wins and sporting legends from cricket, hockey, athletics and more.

questions.q: In which year did India first win the men's Cricket World Cup?
questions.note: Kapil Dev's team beat the West Indies in the final at Lord's.

questions.q: Who was India's first individual Olympic gold medallist?
questions.note: He won the 10 m air rifle event at Beijing 2008.

questions.q: Sachin Tendulkar was the first man to score a double century in a one-day international.
questions.note: He made 200 not out against South Africa in Gwalior in 2010.

questions.q: Which Indian hockey legend is known as The Wizard?
questions.note: National Sports Day, 29 August, marks his birthday.

questions.q: Neeraj Chopra won Olympic gold at Tokyo 2020 in which event?
questions.note: It was India's first Olympic gold in athletics.

questions.q: Viswanathan Anand became a world champion in which sport?
questions.note: In 1988 he became India's first grandmaster.

questions.q: The Indian Premier League (IPL) was first played in 2012.
questions.note: The first IPL season was played in 2008.

questions.q: Who won India's first Olympic medal in badminton?
questions.note: She won bronze in women's singles at London 2012.

questions.q: Which Manipuri boxer, a six-time world champion, won Olympic bronze in 2012?
questions.note: Accept M. C. Mary Kom.

questions.q: What was sprinter Milkha Singh's famous nickname?
questions.note: The film Bhaag Milkha Bhaag (2013) tells his story.

quizzes.title: History & Heritage
quizzes.description: Ancient empires, great temples and the road to independence.

questions.q: Who founded the Maurya Empire?
questions.note: He was guided by his adviser Chanakya, also known as Kautilya.

questions.q: In which year did the Jallianwala Bagh massacre take place in Amritsar?
questions.note: It happened on 13 April 1919, the day of Baisakhi.

questions.q: Gandhi's Dandi March of 1930 was a protest against the British salt tax.
questions.note: He walked about 385 km from Sabarmati Ashram to the coast at Dandi.

questions.q: Babur's victory in which 1526 battle founded the Mughal Empire?
questions.note: Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi, the last Delhi Sultan.

questions.q: The Chinese pilgrim Xuanzang studied at which famous ancient university in Bihar?
questions.note: The ruins of Nalanda Mahavihara are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

questions.q: Who was the first Indian to serve as Governor-General of independent India?
questions.note: He was also the last Governor-General before India became a republic.

questions.q: The Constitution of India came into effect on 15 August 1947.
questions.note: It came into effect on 26 January 1950, now Republic Day.

questions.q: Which Chola king built the Brihadeeswarar Temple at Thanjavur?
questions.note: The temple was completed around 1010 and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

questions.q: Who chaired the Drafting Committee of India's Constitution?
questions.note: Accept Ambedkar or Babasaheb Ambedkar.

questions.q: The 1757 Battle of Plassey was fought against which Nawab of Bengal?
questions.note: Mir Jafar's betrayal helped Robert Clive's East India Company win.
